title: Training Data Provenance Review Pattern
description: A pattern for documenting the source, licence status, and collection method of every dataset used to train a generative model, with an explicit risk decision recorded for any source obtained by scraping copyrighted or trademarked material.
problem: Generative models are often trained on large, aggregated datasets assembled by scraping the public web, with no per-source record of licence status, provenance, or the specific legal risk each source carries — making it difficult to assess or defend the model's commercial deployment when a rights holder objects.
solution: Maintain a per-source log of every dataset used in training, including its origin, collection method, and licence status; for any source obtained by scraping copyrighted or trademarked material, record an explicit risk decision (obtain a licence, exclude the source, or document an accepted-risk rationale) before the model is deployed commercially.
applicability: Any organisation training or fine-tuning a generative model (image, text, audio, or video) intended for commercial deployment.
consequences: Provenance review of web-scale datasets is labour-intensive and may be infeasible to do exhaustively; excluding all uncertain-provenance sources can materially reduce model quality, creating a real tension between legal risk reduction and model performance.

citations.title: Getty Images (US) Inc and others v Stability AI Limited [2025] EWHC 2863 (Ch)
citations.publisher: Courts and Tribunals Judiciary (England and Wales High Court)

relationships.reason: A documented per-source provenance record is the concrete mechanism satisfying this control's data-governance requirement.
The pattern's output is a training data provenance log.
